action.process.end.desc: Ends ONE process chosen in the table. It first asks the program to close as if you clicked X (it can save); it forces the end only if you choose "force" in the confirmation - unsaved work is then lost. Refuses Windows processes, services, security/EDR/VPN/Intune tools and other users' processes (unless administrator).
action.memory.schedule-diagnostic.desc: Opens the Windows Memory Diagnostic (MdSched.exe), which tests RAM on the next restart. There is no documented official way to schedule it without the dialog: you choose "Restart now" or "Check the next time". WinCare never restarts the computer by itself. May show an administrator (UAC) prompt.
section.processes.memory-overview.note: Plain-language status. Limits: available memory below 15% = pressure (below 5% = critical); commit charge from 80% of the limit = pressure (95% = critical; at the limit Windows refuses allocations); page file from 80% = pressure; hard faults (pages read from disk) from 1000 pages/s = pressure. Short sample: repeat to confirm.
section.processes.top-memory.note: Working set = physical RAM in use now; private bytes = memory reserved only by this process. "Service host" lists the Windows services inside the process (e.g. svchost). The command line is not shown because it can contain passwords.
section.processes.growth.note: Heuristic, not proof: private bytes were sampled a few times over a few seconds. "Growing" = rose at every sample, by at least 10 MB and 5%. Programs opening files or filling caches also grow; watch longer before concluding.
section.processes.review.note: Information, not a malware verdict: lists processes running from user-writable folders (Temp, AppData\Roaming, Downloads) or with a missing/invalid digital signature. Many legitimate programs show up here. The signature is checked only on executables outside the Windows folder, up to a limit, with a cache.
section.processes.cpu-now.note: Short sample (two readings of each process's CPU time). 100% = all cores busy. Top 10.
processes.note.no-ram-cleaner: WinCare does not offer "RAM cleaning" (emptying working sets or the standby list). Windows already manages memory: "standby" memory is cache released instantly when a program needs it. Purging it only forces Windows to read everything again from disk and makes the PC slower. What really helps is closing the heavy program (see the tables above) or adding RAM.
processes.threshold.commit: Pressure from {0}%, critical from {1}% of the limit
processes.threshold.compressed: Informative: compression is normal and cheaper than paging
processes.refuse.not-running: The process is no longer running.
processes.refuse.pid-mismatch: The process number now belongs to another program; refresh the list.
processes.refuse.critical-name: Essential Windows process; ending it hangs or crashes the session.
processes.refuse.security-tool: Security, EDR, VPN or management tool (Defender, Intune...): WinCare never touches them.
processes.refuse.hosts-services: Hosts Windows services; use the services manager.
processes.refuse.system-account: Runs as a system account (SYSTEM / LOCAL SERVICE / NETWORK SERVICE).
processes.refuse.other-user: Belongs to another user; only an administrator can end it.
processes.refuse.owner-unknown: The process owner could not be confirmed; run as administrator.
finding.processes-memory-pressure.title: Memory under pressure: {0} = {1}
finding.processes-memory-pressure.recomm: See Processes and memory for the programs using most memory and close the ones you are not using. If it happens all the time, consider more RAM. "RAM cleaners" do not help.
finding.processes-growth-suspect.title: Memory growing steadily: {0} (PID {1}), {2}
finding.processes-growth-suspect.recomme: Heuristic, not proof. Watch the program longer; if it keeps growing until the PC slows down, save your work and restart it or look for an update.
